quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: When driving near a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and be prepared to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down and yield the right-of-way. Be ready to stop to keep the pedestrian safe.

questions.question: Braking distance is affected by:

options.text: The speed your vehicle is traveling.
The condition of your brakes and tires.

questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on three things: how fast you are going, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road.

questions.question: If an officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Copy what other cars are doing.

questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow their directions instead of the traffic light.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to all pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: To help prevent fatigue on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a break on long trips. If you feel sleepy, pull over safely and take a nap or rest for the night.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: Drivers who eat and drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating or drinking while driving takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road. This makes it harder to stay in your lane and control your vehicle.

questions.question: When approaching a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, a driver should yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians with disabilities using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other assistive device have the right-of-way and the same rights as any other pedestrian.

questions.question: Passing is prohibited:

options.text: Whenever a solid line marks the left side of your lane.
When a school bus is stopped to load or unload children on a public road (unless a physical barrier separates traffic).
Off the pavement or shoulder of the road.

questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means no passing. You must stop for a stopped school bus and stay stopped until it moves. You cannot pass on the right if you must leave the pavement to do so.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
Traffic in the lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
Lanes are reserved for buses and vehicles with a driver and one or more passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign marks parking spaces reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn at this location.

questions.question: Cell phones can be a serious source of driver distractions.
questions.explanation: Drivers should not use cell phones while driving, except to report a crash or emergency. Keep your full attention on the road.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrians.
Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to the pedestrians and frighten them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally. Pedestrian safety comes first.

questions.question: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, what must a driver show?
questions.explanation: Drivers must carry and show their license, proof of registration, and proof of insurance. All three documents are required in the vehicle at all times.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must come to a complete stop and yield the right-of-way.
Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield if necessary.
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop. This creates a clear path for the emergency vehicle.

questions.question: You are responsible for ensuring that the vehicle you drive is:
questions.explanation: All vehicles must be registered and carry proof of registration. All vehicles must have insurance. Drivers are responsible for vehicle safety to protect themselves, passengers, and others on the road.

questions.question: Alcohol is the single greatest common factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the leading cause of fatal traffic crashes. It affects vision and slows reaction time. Even small amounts of alcohol impair driving ability.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview and outside mirrors.
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal ahead of time, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If you can, move it out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop severe bleeding. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?
questions.explanation: Driving too fast is a major cause of accidents. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Following too closely causes most rear-end collisions.

questions.question: To protect yourself, do not:

options.text: Drive with a suspended or revoked license.
Lend your driver license to anyone.
Let an unlicensed driver operate your vehicle.

questions.explanation: A person with a suspended or revoked license cannot legally drive. It is illegal to drive without a valid license.

questions.question: To ensure your physical condition does not cause unsafe driving, you should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular check-ups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns drivers that the divided highway is ending ahead.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming hazards and conditions. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign tells drivers there is limited space above.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger directs you to stop.
Flashing red signals and gates are working.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger tells you to or when there is a stop sign. Also stop when you see flashing red signals and gates operating.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
Look both ways as you cross the intersection.
Always come to a full stop at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. You must stop if traffic requires it.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign:

options.text: Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and drive normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs tell drivers a train may be coming. Obey all warning signs and never go around barriers.

questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the streets.
questions.explanation: Drive with extra care where children are present. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Construction workers on or near the roadway.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers of upcoming hazards. This sign warns that pedestrians may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: How should you stay safe when crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
Cross very quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are very dangerous. Always look and listen for trains coming from both directions before crossing. Watch for warning signals and never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Drivers must be careful when passing large vehicles. They should not drive beside large vehicles for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. Do not drive beside a large vehicle for a long time. It is safer to either fall back or move ahead.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights approaches, should the driver pull to the right side of the road and let it pass?
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights and/or sirens approaches, you must pull to the right side of the road right away and let it pass.
